newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force launches navigation satellite.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force launches navigation satellite.

text.p: A McDonnell Douglas Corp Delta 2 rocket was launched on Tuesday night carrying into orbit a U.S. Air Force navigation satellite.
The 12-story-tall unmanned Delta 2 rocket lifted off its Cape Canaveral launch pad at 11:43 p.m. EDT (0343 GMT) with a flash of fire and a thundering roar.
The navigation satellite, built by Lockheed Martin Missiles and Space, was placed into a 12,000 mile (19,200 km) circular orbit about 25 minutes later.

The $43 million spacecraft is the first of a new generation of Global Positioning System satellites to reach orbit. The first satellite in this series was destroyed when a Delta rocket exploded shortly after launch in January.

The 24-satellite Global Position System network allows military users to determine their position anywhere on earth to an accuracy of 30 feet (9 metres) and permits civilians, such as mariners, to calculate their location to within 300 feet (90 metres).
